ORIGIN'S MOVE (1072 -> 1071)

The batching moved out of _write_multi and into _update_rows_sql, and took an arg-type error with it: `for sub_rows in batched(rows, UPDATE_BATCH_SIZE)` handed `_execute_update` a `tuple[tuple, ...]` where its signature says `list[tuple]`, at write.py:240. _write_multi now passes the whole group -- a real list -- and the batched() tuples go to the new _update_rows_values_sql, whose parameter is typed for both. 1072 -> 1071, measured the section 9.3 way: mypy 2.3.0 alone in a fresh venv, --no-incremental, over the six packages, in a worktree at HEAD with only this change applied. HEAD measured 1072 on the same run, so the gate was green before and the move is entirely this change.

THIS BRANCH'S MOVE (1072 -> 1043)

1077 -> 1043, measured with mypy 2.3.0 and NOTHING else installed, on a tree whose only uncommitted work is this change. The floor stood at 1072 and HEAD measured 1077: five errors arrived with 023b1a72b4e, which added odoo/libs/docstring.py and its suite to a package the per-file lock holds at 100%, so raising the floor could not have made py_typecheck green -- exceptions/mypy/libs.txt is shrink-only and the two files were not in it.

FOUR ROOT CAUSES, none of them notation.

  _RegistryStubs claimed an empty __slots__ its subclasses do not keep. _RegistryFieldsMixin and _RegistrySchemaMixin declare none, so a Registry always carries a __dict__ -- models_by_table is a cached_property and three suites read registry.__dict__ directly. A type checker reads each mixin alone, where the whole MRO was slotted, and rejected every self.models = {} / self.has_unaccent = ... in them. Do NOT instead slot the owned names per mixin: two bases with a non-empty __slots__ is a hard TypeError at class creation, verified, and Registry would not import. init_phase went the same way, declared as a writeable attribute while its owner implements it with @property and nothing assigns it.

  Field._by_type__ was declared dict[str, Field] and holds field CLASSES: __init_subclass__ registers cls, registration.py instantiates what it reads back. Spelled builtins.type[Field], because Field declares type: str and that name shadows the builtin for the whole class body.

  _MetricsHost declared only _thread while _record_metrics, which takes self: _MetricsHost, increments self.sql_log_count on every call -- the protocol under-described what the function requires, so any other class satisfying it would have failed at runtime.

  _FieldStubs was missing the value-conversion seam _FieldSqlMixin calls while building a column expression (convert_to_column / convert_to_write / convert_to_cache / _get_cache / column_type / is_temporal / get_company_dependent_fallback). 19 -> 4 in that one file.

Two more were real: register_condition_operators declared Collection[str] while its body makes one pass with frozenset(operators), and test_it_accepts_any_collection has always handed it a generator; and to_sql guards on column_type, which is ("jsonb","jsonb") for a company-dependent field, then indexes _column_type, which the guard does not constrain -- a latent NoneType subscript now raising with its reason.

37 files fell, none rose: error sets diffed line by line against the pre-change run. The per-file lock is green in every package for the first time -- db and libs at 100%, and orm loses its seven standing failures, five regressed files plus _field_sql over budget, which predate the floor commit and were red on a clean HEAD worktree.

Verification: pytest 3727 passed / 1 skipped / 908 subtests, and 1670 passed for the three real-import paths.
